record.context_brief: Global classical well posedness for generic inhomogeneous data
record.original_question: For the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation with a physically meaningful collision kernel, do global classical solutions exist for generic initial data? This is the unconditional global well posedness problem outside perturbative or near-equilibrium regimes.

evidence.quote: For any inhomogeneous model like (2.1), with a nontrivial and physically meaningful collision kernel Q, the global existence of classical solutions for generic initial data f0 remains an outstanding open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation for an unknown nonnegative density f(t,x,v), with t ≥ 0, x ∈ ℝ³ (or 𝕋³) and v ∈ ℝ³:

  ∂_t f + v · ∇_x f = Q(f,f),

where the collision operator Q is the bilinear Boltzmann operator
  Q(f,f)(v) = ∫_{ℝ³} ∫_{S²} B(|v−v_*|, cos θ) [ f(v') f(v_*') − f(v) f(v_*) ] dσ dv_*,
with the standard pre- and post-collisional velocity parametrization
  v' = (v+v_*)/2 + (|v−v_*|/2) σ, v_*' = (v+v_*)/2 − (|v−v_*|/2) σ,
and where B(|v−v_*|, cos θ) is a physically meaningful (nontrivial) collision kernel — for instance a hard-sphere kernel, a hard-potential or soft-potential kernel of the form B = |v−v_*|^γ b(cos θ) with γ ∈ (−3, 1] and either an angular cutoff or a non-cutoff singularity b(cos θ) ∼ θ^{−2−2s} as θ → 0 for some s ∈ (0,1).

Given generic, sufficiently regular and rapidly decaying initial data f_0(x,v) ≥ 0 (not assumed to be a small perturbation of a global Maxwellian equilibrium, nor close to vacuum, nor of small total mass/energy/entropy), prove or disprove that there exists a unique global-in-time classical solution f ∈ C^1([0,∞); suitable function space) of the Cauchy problem f|_{t=0} = f_0.

The question is whether such unconditional global classical well-posedness holds outside perturbative or near-equilibrium regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: The unconditional global existence of classical solutions for the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation with a physically meaningful collision kernel and generic (large) initial data remains a major open problem. Known global results are restricted to renormalized (DiPerna–Lions) weak solutions, perturbative near-Maxwellian regimes, near-vacuum regimes, or special symmetries. No result establishing global classical well-posedness for generic large data has been reported.

status_evidence.title: DiPerna–Lions theory and open problems for Boltzmann
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence of classical solutions for large data remains open; only renormalized weak solutions are known globally (DiPerna–Lions).
status_evidence.claim: Global classical well-posedness for generic large data is open.

status_evidence.title: Villani, A Review of Mathematical Topics in Collisional Kinetic Theory
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of constructing global smooth solutions for arbitrary initial data is widely open.
status_evidence.claim: Open problem status confirmed in standard surveys.
